title: People
markdown:
**What it is:** Everyone the Executive knows about, in two tabs. **Team** is the people who work with you — each with a response SLA, a preferred channel and the approvals they hold. **Contacts** is everyone outside the team — clients, contractors, advisors, or anyone else you deal with — and it is private to you.

**What it does:**

- Add team members with their role, email, and chat IDs (Slack / Discord / Telegram).
- Set a response SLA so the Executive knows when a proposal is overdue.
- Assign **authority scopes** (e.g. approve spend under $10k, sign off on hiring) so proposals route to the right person.
- Mark the principal (you) and set availability or on-leave dates.
- Keep **contacts** so the Executive can email or invite them — but only when you ask it to directly (in the web app, or from your own Slack or Discord). A contact can't sign in, can't message the Executive, never approves anything, and is never chased.
- Keep contacts **private**: only you see them. Nobody else on your team sees the Contacts tab, finds a contact when they ask the Executive, or sees an alert about one.

**Team member or contact?**

| | Team member | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| Signs in to Open Executive (with an email) | Yes | No |
| Messages the Executive on Slack / Discord / Telegram | Yes | No |
| Approves proposals, gets check-ins and reminders | Yes | No |
| The Executive emails or invites them | On any task | Only when you ask directly |
| Who sees them | Everyone on the team | Only you |

**How to use:**

1. Open **People**, pick the **Team** or **Contacts** tab (only you, the principal, see Contacts), and click **+ Add person** (or **+ Add contact**).
2. Choose **Team member** or **Contact** at the top of the dialog, then enter **Full name** (the only required field) and **Role** — for a contact, their role and company (e.g. *Head of Procurement, Acme*) — and their email. If this is you, tick **This is me — Primary** — this can only be set when adding someone, and you are always on the team.
3. For a team member, expand **Contact & routing**: the preferred channel, **Expected reply within *N* hours** (their SLA — default 24), email, and Slack / Discord / Telegram IDs. Those IDs are also what lets this person talk to the Executive on those channels.
4. For a team member, expand **Approval authority** and click each scope they hold:

   | Button | They can approve |
   |---|---|
   | Spend <$2K / <$10K / >$10K | Spend up to that amount (>$10K covers large spend) |
   | Hiring | Hiring sign-off |
   | Vendors | New vendor onboarding |
   | Credit | Customer credits |
   | Legal | Legal signatures |
   | Board | Board communications |
   | All (wildcard) | Anything — the catch-all for approvals no one else is scoped for; usually the principal |

5. Click **Add person** (or **Add contact**). Later, open the person and click **Edit** to set **On leave until**, add **Availability windows** (days, hours, timezone), change their scopes, or move them between team and contacts; **Archive person** retires them from the roster.

**Who can change it:** only the principal can add, edit or archive people — until someone is the principal, whoever sets up first can. Everyone signed in can see the team (your contacts stay yours alone), and teammates can still edit their own working style and mark their open loops done on their page.

**Example from chat:** *"Add Sarah Chen as our fractional CFO — sarah@acme.com — she approves spend under $10k and usually replies within 48 hours."* Or: *"Add Jordan Lee from Acme as a contact — jordan@acme.example — and send them the proposal."* Or open **+ Add person**, press **Ctrl/Cmd + .**, and describe the person — Ask OE fills in the dialog for you to check and save.

**Forward it to the Executive:** forward an email from a client to the Executive's address and it replies to you — not them — with a summary, a draft reply you can send, any dates or commitments, and an offer to add the sender as a contact. Mail a contact sends the Executive directly is summarised for you, never answered on its own. Either way it stays between you and the Executive: it tells no one else, and any alert it raises is yours alone.

**Just for yourself?** When you use Open Executive just for yourself, setup adds only you — marked as the principal, with authority over everything. **People** stays in the sidebar under **You** and opens on **Contacts**: anyone you add from chat is a contact unless you say otherwise, and the **Team** tab shows just you. If you add a team member, Open Executive offers to switch to team mode — or you can keep using it just for yourself. The Briefing doesn't show a People card in this mode.

*Note: authority scopes are how the Executive figures out who on the team to ask for any given approval.*
